fact_sheet.business_description: The Company combines four business units: aftermarket components, automation and warehouse products, industrial software, and productivity systems [D01]. The group is led by CEO Darius Adamczyk and benefits from aftermarket revenue and industrial-safety demand, though it faces diverse cyclicality from oil-and-gas and commercial-aircraft exposures [D01, D03].
economics_vs_peers: Peers include Emerson Electric (23.8x P/E, 3.17% yield), Lockheed Martin (15.3x P/E, 2.53% yield), and Northrop Grumman (19.5x P/E, 1.47% yield) [D04].
Reported group 70-basis-point segment-margin improvement noted in Q1 2017 [D06].

management_board_governance: Prior activist history: not in pack.

gate1.edge_statement: The event is a potential conglomerate breakup of four distinct units where the sum-of-the-parts is obscured by overhead and cyclicality, allowing Third Point to use its constructivist expertise to drive value realization.
gate1.one_line_verdict: a diversified industrial conglomerate with separable business units and a leadership transition window that invites portfolio simplification

gate2.variant_view: The market views the company as a bloated, cyclical conglomerate where the benefits of diversification are offset by structural overhead and complexity, leading to a persistent sum-of-the-parts discount. We believe that under new leadership, a separation of these distinct, high-margin business units will allow the market to re-rate each asset to peer multiples. This transition from a conglomerate structure to focused, pure-play businesses will unlock significant shareholder value that is currently buried in the corporate bureaucracy [D01, D07].

final.memo:
The Company is a diversified industrial conglomerate currently hindered by structural overhead and cyclicality, trading at a persistent discount to its intrinsic sum-of-the-parts [D01, D05]. While the market views the business as a bloated entity, we see four distinct units that, if separated, would be re-rated by the market to trade closer to high-margin peers like Emerson Electric [D04, D07].

Our valuation work, using a conservative 23.8x multiple on estimated enterprise value, suggests a target price of $156.40 per share, implying substantial upside from the recent price of $124.87 [D04]. This valuation is supported by a 5.3% free cash flow yield, which provides a meaningful floor for our investment while we wait for the realization of our thesis [D04].

The market fails to fully credit the underlying quality of the segments, despite the 70-basis-point margin improvement demonstrated in the most recent quarter [D03, D06]. We believe the transition to CEO Darius Adamczyk creates a unique window for a strategic portfolio review, allowing the company to shed unnecessary complexity and align its margins with industry leaders [D01, D07].

We intend to engage constructively with the board and management to advocate for this portfolio simplification over the next two quarters [D01, D04]. Should this private engagement fail to yield a commitment to a strategic review, we are prepared to escalate our efforts, including a potential public letter and nomination of board candidates [D01, D05].

We acknowledge risks regarding tax and pension liabilities as well as cyclical headwinds in oil and aerospace, but we remain confident that a structural separation serves the best interests of shareholders [D05, D06]. Our decision is to initiate a position with a 5% initial allocation of NAV, with a target to build to 8% as our engagement progresses [D05].
